trials.claim: Seller promises lifetime access to the Monthly1K Course
trials.claimQuote: Get lifetime access to the Monthly1K Course now!
trials.reasoning: A buyer reports never being able to access the purchased course, and Teachable's terms allow termination of services at any time without notice, materially limiting lifetime access.

exhibits.quote: I bought this course in 2023 but could never even access the course on Teachable with my email.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports being unable to access the course at all despite purchase, contradicting lifetime access.

exhibits.quote: Teachable may modify, terminate, or refuse to provide Teachable Services at any time for any reason, without notice.
exhibits.argument: Platform reserves right to terminate services without notice, undermining any promise of lifetime access.

trials.claimQuote: Normally, this course would cost you $600 (which you should make back in the first month).
trials.reasoning: Buyers paying $10 or $1 in promotions does not show the course's normal price was not $600, and no exhibit states its regular price.

exhibits.quote: Whether this is a scam or not, it was $10 !! That's cheaper than a book.
exhibits.argument: Buyer paid $10, undermining claim that course normally costs $600.

exhibits.quote: When I saw the $1 price tag from Noah, it was a no-brainer to purchase.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports $1 price tag, contradicting $600 normal price.

trials.claim: Course offered for just $49 right now
trials.claimQuote: But right now, we’re offering it for just $49.
trials.reasoning: Reports of paying $10 or $7 at other times do not establish the price offered 'right now' in the seller's offer, so the $49 claim cannot be verified either way.

exhibits.quote: decent course, picked up a few things - can't really complain for $10 however, it could definitely do with updating.
exhibits.argument: Buyer paid $10 not $49, showing the just $49 price is misleading.

exhibits.quote: The BEST part is obviously the RIDICULOUS price point! $7 is laughable.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports paying $7, contradicting the claim it is offered for just $49 right now.

trials.claim: Course walks step-by-step from idea to successful business in less than one month even if not an expert
trials.claimQuote: Monthly1K is an online course that walks you step-by-step from idea to successful business in less than one month (even if you're not an expert).
trials.reasoning: A buyer reports getting toward their first three customers within 48 hours and another calls the course super-easy to follow, directly supporting a step-by-step course usable by non-experts in under a month.

exhibits.quote: It’s really basic and in dire need of an update. The date in the screen from the videos is 2012!
exhibits.argument: Buyer says content is basic and from 2012, undermining step-by-step to successful business claim.

exhibits.quote: The course is also very long and it takes forever to get through the course.
exhibits.argument: Buyer says course takes forever, contradicting promise of idea to business in less than one month.

exhibits.quote: As advertised, within 48 hours of starting I'd overcome a couple of mind-blocks that I'd had since my childhood, on the way to getting my first three customers.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms getting customers within 48 hours, supporting the less-than-one-month business-building promise.

exhibits.quote: The course is super-easy to follow, FUN and the other course peeps are solid in the chat.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms the course is super-easy to follow, supporting that non-experts can follow it step-by-step.

trials.claim: Seller promises techniques can be repeated to get $1,000+ in recurring revenue for life
trials.claimQuote: The techniques learned here can be repeated to get you $1,000+ in recurring revenue for life.
trials.reasoning: The defense reviews express confidence or vague expectations of making money, but none shows actually achieving $1,000+ in recurring revenue, let alone for life.

exhibits.quote: There is not much substance to this. The information presented can be absorbed in a couple of hours, there is no need for a monthly subscription and especially not a yearly one.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports no substance and no need for subscription, undermining $1,000+ recurring revenue for life claim.

exhibits.quote: I only regret the time I spent going through the entire thing hoping there would be some value in it.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports no value after completing course, contradicting promise of repeatable revenue techniques.

exhibits.quote: I'm confident that if I stick to the course I will get the 1k a month I dream of.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms expecting $1k a month from sticking to the course, supporting the recurring revenue claim.

exhibits.quote: anyone who uses this course can AND will make my $$ before they even finish if they actually DO IT
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms users can make money from the course techniques if they apply them.

trials.claim: Buyer gets access to Monthly1k Facebook community to ask questions and stay accountable
trials.claimQuote: you also get access to the Monthly1k community on Facebook to ask questions, share your wins, organize mastermind calls, and keep each other accountable.
trials.reasoning: A buyer says the community is built into the course instead of requiring Facebook, which conflicts with the promised Facebook community, and the defense exhibits only confirm generic networking or chat, not Facebook access.

exhibits.quote: the class community is built in, so you can take action and respond right after the lesson Instead of having to log out and go to Facebook.
exhibits.argument: Buyer says community is built-in instead of Facebook, undermining Facebook community access claim.

exhibits.quote: The course asks for a lot of engagement in the comment section but appears to rely on feedback from peers instead of the people offering the course.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports engagement relies on peers not course staff, undermining promised supportive community.

exhibits.quote: I think the most value there is in the course is the ability to network with like-minded people.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms the course provides valuable networking with like-minded people, supporting the community access promise.

exhibits.quote: The course is super-easy to follow, FUN and the other course peeps are solid in the chat.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms interacting with other course members in chat, supporting an active community.
